radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Date: 15 Feb 2025 | Facility: Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem
Clinical indication: Assessment prompted by escalating PSA at 3.0 ng/mL, velocity 0.78 ng/mL/yr, and previous negative biopsy.

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 25.0 mL in volume. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates an asymmetric hypointense focus within the left mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging reveals marked restriction with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early focal enhancement. No extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring approximately 8 x 6 mm. PSAD 0.12 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.7542332.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical follow-up addressed ongoing PSA elevation, currently recorded at 2.1 ng/mL subsequent to a prior negative biopsy. Discussion centered on repeat testing alongside clinical correlation. Owing to the upward trajectory and past biopsy results, a urology outpatient clinic visit was arranged for further assessment.
